explicit_propositions.text: We leave Washington, D.C., early each year, right before the August recess.
Congress passes a Continuing Resolution (CR) instead of a full budget.
The August recess is a month-long break during which members of Congress typically return to their districts.
The national debt has reached $35 trillion.
A Continuing Resolution allows federal spending to continue at previous levels without requiring justification.
Passing a full budget would require scrutiny of individual spending programs, many of which may no longer exist.
The U.S. has not passed a formal budget in over 30 years.
Families, schools, churches, and local governments all use budgets to manage finances.
The U.S. government spends money it does not have and relies on printing more currency to cover deficits.
Debt increases by approximately one trillion dollars every hundred days due to current fiscal policies.

assumptions.text: Budgeting is a fundamental practice of responsible financial behavior, applicable to both individuals and institutions.
The failure to pass a budget reflects moral and institutional failure rather than procedural complexity.
Continuing Resolutions are inherently dishonest mechanisms that shield wasteful spending from accountability.
The Speaker of the House lacks consistent control over the majority party’s unity, undermining legislative effectiveness.
Republican lawmakers who support certain bills despite personal disagreement are betraying core conservative principles.
Voters understand the importance of holding elected officials accountable based on policy consistency and integrity.
Elections serve as a mechanism for restoring ideological purity within the Republican Party.
The American public expects representatives to prioritize legislative duty over political conventions and leisure travel.
The Secret Service and other agencies failed to act effectively during the attempted assassination of Donald Trump.
Public trust in governmental institutions is eroded by contradictory official narratives and lack of transparency.
